action_history.rationale: Step 0 of 10 with only 5 initial points in 2D — the surrogate is severely undertrained. With 100% of the budget remaining, investing 1-2 steps in pure exploration via max_variance will build a much better model of the landscape before switching to log_ei for exploitation. The current best y=7.40 is noted but the GP cannot reliably guide search yet with so few points. Default kernel/noise settings are appropriate given no evidence of jaggedness or high noise.

Budget is 90% remaining (9 of 10 steps left) with only 6 data points in 2D — still severely undertrained. The previous max_variance step failed to sample at the true acquisition peak (placed candidate at x1≈-0.5 instead of x1≈5 where variance was highest), so the exploration gap persists. One more max_variance step is warranted to properly cover the unexplored high-x1 region before switching to log_ei. Switching to matern_1.5 because the strongly 1D landscape (x1 Sobol=1.0, x2=0.0) with only 6 points may exhibit sharp variation that a rougher kernel captures better. min_noise_low is kept since the LOO residual issue stems from data sparsity, not measurement noise. After this step (with 8 remaining), I will transition to log_ei for exploitation.

Two max_variance exploration steps have been completed, covering both the low-x1 and high-x1 regions of the dominant axis (x1 Sobol≈1.0). The model now has 7 points spanning the input space and LOO-CV passes. With 8 steps remaining (80% budget), it is time to transition from pure exploration to balanced optimization via log_ei, which will direct sampling toward regions likely to improve upon the current best y≈4.57 while still accounting for uncertainty. Returning to matern_2.5 as the default kernel since the landscape appears smooth along the dominant x1 axis and LOO-CV showed no issues. min_noise_low is retained as there is no evidence of measurement noise.

LOO-CV failed with point 5 residual at ~2× the band, and several other points near band edges — the GP is overfitting local variation. Switching to matern_1.5 to accommodate the rougher landscape (consistent with the now-apparent x1×x2 interactions, Sobol sum >1). Raising noise floor to min_noise_med to regularize the fit and reduce sensitivity to individual points. With 7 steps remaining (70% budget) and 8 data points spanning the space after 2 exploration rounds, log_ei provides the right balance of exploitation toward the current best (y=3.16) and uncertainty-guided exploration. The problem is more complex than initially estimated (both inputs matter with interactions), so the improved surrogate calibration should yield better-targeted candidates.

Following diagnostic recommendations from step 4: switching to matern_2.5 + min_noise_high to address persistent LOO-CV failures where multiple points exceed the uncertainty band by 2-3×. The GP has been overfitting individual observations, producing unreliable acquisition landscapes. min_noise_high (floor 1e-2) will force the GP to smooth its mean function, reducing sensitivity to individual data points and improving surrogate calibration. matern_2.5 provides the right balance of smoothness for this landscape with x1×x2 interactions. With 6 steps remaining (60% budget) and a current best of y=3.16 that has been improving, log_ei provides balanced exploitation toward the best region while maintaining uncertainty-guided exploration. The priority is fixing model calibration so subsequent steps are well-directed.

LOO-CV has failed for 3 consecutive steps across multiple kernel/noise combinations (matern_1.5/low, matern_2.5/high, matern_1.5/med), and Sobol sensitivity indices have flip-flopped dramatically (x1 dominance: 1.0→0.67→0.80→0.42; x2: 0.0→0.44→0.27→0.68). This inconsistency strongly signals non-stationarity — different regions of the landscape have different effective length scales. Input warping (Kumaraswamy) will allow the GP to adaptively rescale axes, addressing the root cause rather than cycling through kernel/noise settings. Using matern_1.5 per latest diagnostic suggestion for the rough landscape with interactions, and min_noise_low to let the GP learn noise freely rather than forcing a floor. With 5 steps remaining (50% budget) and best y=3.16 still improving, log_ei provides the right exploitation/exploration balance.

LOO-CV has failed for 4 consecutive steps across multiple kernel/noise combos (matern_1.5/low, matern_2.5/high, matern_1.5/med, matern_1.5/low+warp). The wildly flip-flopping Sobol indices (x1: 1.0→0.67→0.80→0.42→0.34; x2: 0.0→0.44→0.27→0.68→0.76) are strong evidence of non-stationarity. Keeping warp (one step is insufficient to evaluate it) while switching to matern_2.5 per diagnostic suggestion — this kernel may better balance smoothness with the warped coordinates. min_noise_med provides moderate regularization without over-smoothing like min_noise_high did. With 4 steps remaining (40% budget), log_ei provides the right exploitation/exploration balance to drive y toward lower values.

Budget = 3: must exploit. After 4 consecutive LOO-CV failures across multiple kernel/noise combos, step 5's combination of matern_2.5 + warp + min_noise_med finally achieved a passing LOO-CV. The warp successfully addresses the non-stationarity that plagued earlier fits (evidenced by wildly flip-flopping Sobol indices now stabilizing at x1=0.90, x2=0.26). The acquisition surface shows a well-defined exploitative peak with the candidate correctly placed on it. With a calibrated model and only 3 steps remaining, log_ei is the ideal choice — it will direct sampling toward the minimum (current best y=1.148) while respecting remaining uncertainty. Changing the model configuration now would risk losing calibration and wasting precious budget.

Budget = 2: strong exploitation required. The matern_2.5 + warp + min_noise_med configuration achieved passing LOO-CV for 2 consecutive steps after 4 failures — this is the first stable, calibrated model we've had. The warp successfully addresses the non-stationarity that caused wildly flip-flopping Sobol indices and persistent LOO-CV failures across all other kernel/noise combinations. Current best y=1.148 with clear recent improvement (from 3.16). Changing any model setting now risks losing calibration and wasting one of our final 2 shots. log_ei on a well-calibrated model will direct sampling toward the true minimum with appropriate uncertainty-awareness. This is the textbook scenario for log_ei: calibrated surrogate + low budget + active improvement trend.

FINAL experiment (budget=1): maximum exploitation required. UCB with beta=0.1 aggressively targets the predicted minimum near current best y=1.148. Retaining warp transform because it was the key breakthrough that resolved 4 consecutive LOO-CV failures — removing it risks reverting to the unstable surrogate. Keeping matern_2.5 which paired well with warp for the only passing LOO-CV steps. Switching from min_noise_med to min_noise_low to allow the GP to fit tightly around the best-found region, maximizing precision of the exploitation target. This configuration prioritizes the most accurate possible prediction of where the true minimum lies, directing our single remaining shot there.
